composers_checked.name: Jenkins, John
composers_checked.note: Fantasias, pavans and In Nomines a 4, 5 and 6, eleven works for treble(s), basses and organ, Newark Siege, the Five Bell Consort; the airs and three-part fantasias not matched

note: All eight composers are English Renaissance/Jacobean; their era is given as 'baroque' because the vocabulary has no Renaissance era. Floor evidence is Apple Music track lists of consort recordings (Phantasm, Fretwork, Hespèrion, Rose Consort, Hathor, London Baroque ...); where a recording numbers pieces differently from IMSLP's VdGS numbers and no concordance was found, the pages are skipped as 'not checked (numbering not matched to a recording)' rather than guessed. Ward: IMSLP gives VdGS 13 for both 'Leggiadra sei' and 'Non fu senze'; Phantasm (Linn) numbers 'Non fu senze' VdGS 14, used here. Byrd: the eleven consort songs added by the gap check are recorded with viols (Fretwork/Kirkby, Concordia/Blaze, Ricercar, Ensemble Orlando Gibbons); the 1588 ones are on IMSLP as five-voice songs, which the census left out as vocal; voice-and-four-viols scoring assumed from those recordings. Tomkins: the five-part Pavans Nos. 6 and 7 are matched to VdGS 6 and 7 by number only (low confidence); Phantasm may use the Musica Britannica numbering, as it does for the three-part fantasias. Gibbons: the nine pages of the Fantazies of III Parts (VdGS 2.1-2.9) were left out by the census as 'unspecified instruments'; they are covered by the set entry. The Cries of London are entered as five viols with the voices doubling the parts (IMSLP: '5 viols and partly 5 voices colla parte'). Lawes: IMSLP's 'Suite No. N for 2 Viols and Organ' and 'for 3 Viols and Organ' pages are the Fantasia-Suites for one and two violins, bass viol and organ (Folop scores the violin parts for treble viol); entered with the original scoring. IMSLP gives D-flat for the six-part B-flat Sett. The Royall Consort and Harp Consorts were added from recordings (no IMSLP candidate); the Harp Consorts recorded only in part are entered without a duration. Jenkins: the 4-part fantasias follow Fretwork's complete recording (keys from Phantasm); the 5-part numbering is confirmed as VdGS by Phantasm's keys (VdGS 2 in G minor, 7 in C minor, as IMSLP); the 6-part and the fantasia-suites and divisions for treble(s), basses and organ were added from Phantasm and Fretwork (some may sit on IMSLP's 'Airs for 4 Viols with Organ' page unmatched). Newark Siege: IMSLP's date 'after 1546' should read 1646. Not covered: the airs, three-part fantasias, Newberry Aires and the Fantasia-Air sets (Locke Consort, VdGS VII:1-15). Dowland: the census left out the separate pages of the Lachrimae pieces as 'unspecified instruments'; the print names viols or violins, so the reason is wrong, but they are covered by the set entry. Open: Jenkins's airs, three-part fantasias, fantasia-suites and Fantasia-Air sets; Tomkins's fantasias; Ward's 4-part fantasias 'in Paris'; Byrd's Fantasias a 4 Nos. 2, 4, 5. A VdGS thematic-index concordance would settle most of them.
